note_on_method: Two of the filter slugs have a lawful data driver in Tampa, and the same fact drives both. The City's pickleball page labels every outdoor card "Outdoor Pickleball" and puts the community-centre courts under a heading that reads "Indoor Pickleball", so indoor and outdoor are stated, in the City's own words, for all sixteen published venues. Lights has no driver: the City states no lighting for any venue. Free has none: the City states no price for any court, and the one "free" on the page is a beginner lesson.

slots.why_this_filter:
Twelve Tampa venues hold outdoor pickleball courts, and forty-five of the city's fifty-two courts are at them. What earns the page a URL of its own is that the City drew the line itself. Every one of those twelve cards carries the label "Outdoor Pickleball" (at Davis Islands, "Outdoor pickleball") and the community-centre courts sit apart under a heading that reads "Indoor Pickleball". Tampa is one of the largest cities on this site where the operator states it for every published venue.

The practical reason to filter is that the two kinds of venue are documented in opposite ways. The indoor courts come with session schedules and phone numbers. The outdoor courts mostly come with a count and an address: nine of the twelve say nothing about hours, and none says anything about lighting, price or surface. The largest sets are outdoors, Macfarlane's eight and six each at Cuscaden and Julian B Lane, and the only scheduled outdoor session in the city is Cuscaden's "Senior open play Wed 9-11 am".
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City's pickleball page lists it under the label "Outdoor Pickleball" with a court count. Twelve qualify: Al Barnes Park, Copeland Park, Cuscaden Park, Davis Islands, Forest Hills, Highland Pines Park, Julian B Lane Riverfront Park, Macfarlane Park, Madison Street Park, New Tampa Sports Pavilion, Skyview Park and Vila Brothers Park.

Three need a word. Forest Hills qualifies on its two outdoor courts and appears on the indoor page as well, because the City lists a second card at the same address. Davis Islands qualifies with "2 multi-purpose courts", the City's own word, kept rather than promoted to pickleball courts. The New Tampa Sports Pavilion qualifies because the City labels its card outdoor, and nothing on either City page says its courts are under a roof. Two outdoor venues the City lists cannot be published: Rowlett Park, eight courts at an address neither resolver finds, and Foster Park, two courts at an address the Census flips to the other side of the city.

faqs.q: Which outdoor courts in Tampa have lights?
faqs.a: The City does not say, for any venue. Not one outdoor card mentions lighting, so every venue on this page is recorded as not stated rather than lit or unlit.

faqs.q: Which outdoor venues state their hours?
faqs.a: Three. Madison Street Park and Vila Brothers Park are "Open daily from sunrise to sunset"; the New Tampa Sports Pavilion is open Monday-Friday 4:30-9 pm and Saturday-Sunday 8 am-9 pm. The other nine carry no hours.
Not stated. The City publishes no price for any court, and a park court is not assumed free because no fee was written down.

slots.why_this_filter:
Five Tampa venues hold indoor pickleball courts, seven courts between them, and the City puts every one of them under a heading that reads "Indoor Pickleball". Tampa has more published indoor venues than any city on this site except Wichita, and its indoor page is one of only a few on the site.

None of the five is an indoor pickleball facility. Four are community centres (Barksdale, Cordelia B Hunt, Loretta Ingraham and Port Tampa) and the fifth, Forest Hills, is a community centre sharing its address with a park holding two outdoor courts. In each, the courts exist at the session times the City prints and, so far as the record shows, not otherwise. Two cards say "Play resumes after Summer Camp ends", one says "Court closed for repairs through June 1", and none of the dates carries a year on a page dated 28 October 2025. An indoor venue here is a place to play in a known window, with a phone number to confirm it, rather than a place to turn up.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City's pickleball page lists it under the heading "Indoor Pickleball" with a court count. Five qualify: Forest Hills with two, Loretta Ingraham Center with two, and David M Barksdale Center, Cordelia B Hunt Center and Port Tampa Community Center with one each, seven indoor courts in all. Port Tampa qualifies although its card says the court was "closed for repairs through June 1": the count is stated, and the closure is printed beside it as the City printed it.

The Dr Martin Luther King Jr. Complex is on the City's indoor list with two courts and a schedule the City marks as not yet set. It is refused because the City prints two house numbers for it (220 N Oregon Ave on the pickleball page, 2200 on the recreation-centres page) and the one carrying the count resolves to a postcode the City's own pages contradict. The Copeland Park Center has a gymnasium on the recreation-centres list and no indoor pickleball on the City's page, so Copeland is an outdoor venue only, as is Highland Pines. A gym is not an indoor court until the operator counts one there.

faqs.q: When can I play indoors in Tampa?
faqs.a: At the session times the City prints: weekday afternoons at Barksdale, Monday and Friday evenings at Loretta Ingraham, Tuesday and Thursday evenings at Cordelia B Hunt and Port Tampa, and Monday, Wednesday and Friday at Forest Hills.
Not stated. The City prices no court in Tampa. The Monday beginner lessons at Barksdale are stated as free, but that is a lesson, not the court.

faqs.q: Is the Port Tampa court open?
faqs.a: The City's card says "Court closed for repairs through June 1" with no year. Ring 813-832-1215 before going.
